sub1: A 24-line design supplied as a grid — cover weeks at 1, 7, 12 and 18, and the midday turn re-timed to 12:00–20:30
sub3: What this design keeps of today, and where the December 2026 headcounts differ
coverNote: gaps of 7, 6, 5, 6 around the wheel — close to even, one line out
sub7: Checkable rather than reproducible: there is no search behind it, and every figure is computed from the cells
method:
1 · It was supplied, not searched. This rotation arrived as a Word table with the cover week moved from 17 to 18 and the midday turn re-timed to 12:00–20:30. It was read straight into the app's own shape and judged; no table was enumerated for it and no grid annealed, so there is no search to reproduce. What can be reproduced is every figure on these pages.

2 · The reading was checksummed before anything was built on it. A grid read from a document can carry a silent transcription error, so the duty minutes were totalled against the contract first: Monday to Saturday comes to 42,000 minutes against 20 working lines × 35h = 42,000, exactly. A misread digit would almost certainly have shown up there.

3 · The judge is the workspace's own — runDesignChecks, weeklyHours, assessHardLimits, assessFatigue, scoreOrder and calcHourlyCoverage, with nothing typed by hand and nothing softened. Where the design misses one of the December 2026 timetable rules the table opposite says so rather than omitting the row.
openQuestions: Every hard gate is clear — 35h to the minute, no rest under 12 hours, no hard-limit breach, and the worst-case run of nine days is inside Chiltern's thirteen. What is left is advisory, and there is more of it than in the other proposals here. Five ORR factors are present, and two are the ones to look at: FF11 at 16 shifts without a 48-hour break, against a threshold of 13 and the highest of any design assessed so far; and MRSF at 60.6 hours in a seven-day period against 55. The longest run is nine days — inside the limit, but above the design target of seven. Only 6 of the 20 working lines are a single turn, so most weeks ask somebody to hold more than one start time; that is what drives FF19 to seven. None of this needs a duty to change. Every one of those five is a property of which week sits next to which, not of the staffing — on the two designs already searched this way the same shape work took the factors from five to one and the run from nine to six with the coverage curve untouched. The cover spread is also one line out (7, 6, 5, 6), which the same search fixes for free.
